clue.text: High-risk entertaining the queen's court

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to hold them within, so the risky word takes the royal letters inside it

parts.note: chancy means risky, uncertain
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen

explanation.surface: A dangerous gamble of hosting the monarch's royal household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' looks like the royal court that the queen keeps, but it is the law court.
explanation.definitionFit: Chancery was a division of the English High Court of Justice, so it is a court of law.

clue.text: Tom, say, catches nude show

indicators.note: one word catches another by holding it inside

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, so it's an example
bare means naked

explanation.surface: A peeping tom catches sight of a naked performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' looks like a man's name or a peeping Tom, but it is a male cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabaret is a nightclub entertainment of songs, dances and sketches, a kind of show.

clue.text: Scottish town's broadcast on the radio

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', a link to what follows

indicators.note: radio is heard not read, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: to air is to broadcast

explanation.surface: A Scottish town is being talked about on a radio programme.
explanation.walkthrough: Ayr is a town on the west coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayr is a coastal town in south-west Scotland, home of a racecourse.

clue.text: Rider's shout of joy suppressing a scream

indicators.note: holding something down inside, so the cry contains the other letters

parts.note: a cheer is a joyful shout
the article taken as it stands
a riot or a scream is something hilarious

explanation.surface: A rider stifles a scream inside a cry of delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A scream' and 'a riot' both mean a very funny person or thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A charioteer is the driver of a chariot, so one who rides in it.

clue.text: Farm sector loses leader

indicators.note: the word drops its first letter, the one at the front

parts.note: a branch is a division or sector

explanation.surface: A farming industry sector loses its chief.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranch is a large farm, especially one raising cattle in the Americas.

clue.text: Nag with repeated notes read aloud

indicators.note: repeated means the note sounds twice over, one after the other
read aloud means the letters are taken by how they are spoken

parts.note: G is a musical note, its letter name said gee; two of them give GG

explanation.surface: Someone nags while reading out the same musical notes again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: Say the note G twice and you have the child's word for a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Gee-gee is a childish or slang word for a horse, and a nag is an old horse.

clue.text: Need to change prime minister

indicators.note: the four letters are altered in order

parts.note: the word itself supplies the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A call for a change of national leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Anthony Eden was British Prime Minister from 1955 to 1957.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Anthony Eden served as UK prime minister, succeeding Churchill in 1955.

clue.text: Rookie footballer is an employee of course!

parts.note: green means inexperienced, new
a goalkeeper, often just called a keeper

explanation.surface: A new player is of course on the team's payroll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course!' looks like an exclamation of obviousness; it means employed at a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: A greenkeeper is employed to maintain a golf course and its greens.

clue.text: Treaty port nearly covering up chaos

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means read from the bottom, backwards
the words conceal the answer within them

parts.note: the run of letters spans the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A trading port almost hides disorder from view.
explanation.definitionFit: Entropy is the measure of disorder in a system, so it stands for chaos or decline.

clue.text: Music style picked up pop jargon

indicators.note: lifted upward, which in a down entry reverses the word

parts.note: rap is a genre of music
to lance a boil is to pop it

explanation.surface: A musical genre adopting pop's slang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' looks like a homophone signal, but here it raises the word, reversing it in the down light; 'pop' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Parlance is a particular way of speaking, the vocabulary of a group, i.e. its jargon.

clue.text: Cheap pub to bring in wicked blokes ahead of time

indicators.note: the men come before the time letter in the answer, placed in front of it

parts.note: a bar is a drinking place
to gain is to earn or bring in money
base means morally low
men; bloke is British slang for a man

explanation.surface: A cheap pub hoping to attract bad lads early in the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Bargain-basement describes goods sold at very low prices, like a store's cut-price lower floor.

clue.text: Mixing up Torah and Bible creates a bewildering situation

indicators.note: jumbling the two holy books together so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: the Jewish scripture's name supplies its letters as written
the Christian scripture's name supplies its letters as written

explanation.surface: Muddling two sacred scriptures together leads to confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the two book names are rearranged; 'and' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: From Alice in Wonderland, going down a rabbit hole means entering a strange, disorienting state of affairs.

clue.text: Vocally expresses disapproval of sailors' drunken voyage

indicators.note: vocally means by voice, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: expresses disapproval is boos; sailors are crews, so the words give boos crews

explanation.surface: Someone loudly objects to the sailors going on a boozy trip.
explanation.walkthrough: BOOS and CREWS spoken together give the trip's name. A booze cruise is a British day trip across the Channel to buy cheap alcohol in France.
explanation.definitionFit: A booze cruise is a sea trip, often a ferry run, taken mainly to drink or stock up on alcohol.

clue.text: About to get brief details

indicators.note: cut short, so the phrase loses its last letter

parts.note: to be in for something is to be about to get it, as in 'in for a shock'

explanation.surface: Someone about to receive a short summary of the particulars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief details' reads as one phrase, but 'brief' trims the phrase before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Info is a casual shortening of information, meaning facts or particulars.

clue.text: Awfully energetic around a relative

indicators.note: the scrambled word goes round the single letter
done badly, so the word is scrambled

parts.note: the word itself is the fodder to be scrambled
the article taken as it stands

explanation.surface: A frightfully lively relation fussing about.
explanation.definitionFit: A great-niece is the granddaughter of one's sibling, a family member.

clue.text: Ran with Del Boy, perhaps, almost getting diamonds

indicators.note: nearly all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: Del Boy is Derek Trotter of the BBC sitcom Only Fools and Horses, so he is an example of a Trotter

explanation.surface: A character from a TV comedy running off with stolen jewels.
explanation.walkthrough: Del Boy is the wheeler-dealer hero of the British sitcom Only Fools and Horses; his surname is Trotter. D is the card abbreviation for diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: To trot is to run at a moderate pace, so trotted is a past-tense synonym for ran.

clue.text: Computers from the French, a thousand at most

parts.note: des is French for 'of the' or 'from the'
K, from kilo, stands for a thousand
tops means at most, as in 'two hours tops'

explanation.surface: French machines costing a thousand at the most.
explanation.definitionFit: Desktops are personal computers designed to sit on a desk.

clue.text: Room in northern Surrey to wander

indicators.note: letters that wander move about, so the county name is rearranged

parts.note: the county name supplies the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A spot in the north of Surrey for a stroll.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is a county south of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursery is a room in a house set aside for babies or young children.

clue.text: Unhelpful instruction for conserving something?

wordplay.note: split in two, this is a command to economise: employ a smaller amount

explanation.surface: A not-very-useful command about saving resources.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words to get an order to economise; joined up it means futile.
explanation.definitionFit: Something useless is of no practical help, serving no purpose.

clue.text: Employed to secure luck, like a horseshoe

indicators.note: to hold fast within, so one word is set inside the other

parts.note: used means put to work
hap is an old word for chance or luck

explanation.surface: A lucky horseshoe used to ensure good fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: A horseshoe's curved outline resembles the letter U, so it is U-shaped.

clue.text: Paper with unfinished petition, for instance

parts.note: an exam paper is a test

indicators.note: not completed, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a plea is an earnest request

explanation.surface: An exam paper combined with an incomplete appeal, to give an illustration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For instance' looks like a phrase introducing an illustration; here 'for' is a link and 'instance' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a single case illustrating a general point, which is what an example is.

clue.text: Old wood put on walls of library

indicators.note: in a down entry, the first part sits on top of the second

parts.note: elder is a shrub or tree, and its wood

indicators.note: the outer letters, like a building's walls

parts.note: its first and last letters form the walls

explanation.surface: Timber used to panel a library's walls.
explanation.definitionFit: Elderly means advanced in years, so aged or old.

clue.text: Unlimited wine for chap in Cologne?

indicators.note: without its limits, the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: sherry is a fortified wine from Spain

explanation.surface: A man in a German city drinks wine without restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unlimited wine' looks like free-flowing drink; it means trimming both ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Herr is the German title for a man, the equivalent of Mr, so a German gentleman.

clue.text: Half-heartedly holding back cool old city

indicators.note: the word's double heart is halved, losing one of its two middle letters

parts.note: stalling is delaying or holding back
rad is slang for cool, excellent

explanation.surface: Someone half-heartedly delaying a cool response.
explanation.walkthrough: The doubled L in the middle of the delaying word is its heart; halving it leaves one.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalingrad was the Soviet name for the Russian city now called Volgograd, scene of a famous WWII battle.

clue.text: Slowly advanced over top of obstacle

indicators.note: in a down entry, the first part sits above the next

parts.note: lent as in advanced money

indicators.note: the topmost, first letter of the word

parts.note: its first letter sits at the top

explanation.surface: Advancing slowly over the top of a hurdle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advanced' looks like moving forward but means lending money.
explanation.definitionFit: Lento is a musical tempo marking meaning to be played slowly.

clue.text: Charm — it's missing from cocktail

indicators.note: the pronoun is absent from the drink, so its letters are removed

parts.note: a mojito is a rum cocktail
the pronoun 'it', with the 's as 'is' linking

explanation.surface: The appeal is lost when a mixed drink lacks something.
explanation.definitionFit: Mojo is magical power or personal magnetism, a synonym of charm.

clue.text: Rewritten epistle torn open — you won't like what it says!

definitions.text: you won't like what it says!

indicators.note: written again in a different way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: all three words supply the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A letter rewritten and ripped open whose contents will upset you.
explanation.definitionFit: A poison-pen letter is an anonymous malicious missive meant to wound or threaten its recipient.

clue.text: Rubbish bit of needlework?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to make tatting, a knotted lace

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the needlework sense is a verb for making lace rather than a piece of sewing.
explanation.definitionFit: Tat means cheap tasteless junk, and tatting is a lacework craft done with a shuttle.

clue.text: Drink knocked back before working is a spirit

indicators.note: the reversed drink comes first in the answer
drunk down and also turned backwards, so the drink is reversed

parts.note: mead is a honey-based alcoholic drink
on as in switched on, operating

explanation.surface: Downing a drink before work is a spirited act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' is drinker's slang for downing a drink, and here also signals reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A daemon is a supernatural being or guiding genius in Greek myth, a kind of spirit.

clue.text: Witches put a strain on city

parts.note: a coven is a gathering of witches
to try someone is to test their patience

explanation.surface: A gathering of witches puts pressure on a town.
explanation.walkthrough: Coventry is a city in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Coventry is a city in the West Midlands of England.
